text:
Alex: Heads-up — saw a regression on the seqlen-aware kernel path after the driver restart this morning.  p50 tokens/sec dropped ~18% for 128-256 bins.
Meera: ugh, when was the restart and which nodes? any logs?
Alex: restart was 04:12 UTC on service-gpu-a. infra-bot posted the restart: 
infra-bot: service-gpu-a restarted by auto-recover at 2026-03-18T04:12:07Z (reason: OOM on kernel-tuner process)
Samir: can you paste the perf probe? did autotuner pick a different kernel or fall back to generic matmul?
Alex: attaching short profile snippet from the tail of the workload run: 
```
# profile summary (sampled)
seqbin:128-256  kernel_choice: aten_fp16_cuda      avg_ms: 3.9  count: 12k
seqbin:128-256  kernel_choice: gen_kernels_v2     avg_ms: 4.6  count: 8k
seqbin:64-127   kernel_choice: aten_fp16_cuda      avg_ms: 2.1  count: 20k
cache_hit_rate: overall 0.72   kv_prefix_hits: 0.81
```
Alex: autotuner seems to have biased toward gen_kernels_v2 after restart for those bins. cache hit rate dipped slightly too.
Meera: that explains perf. When driver restarts we currently drop the in-memory kernel affinity table and re-probe starting with a cold heuristic. The default probelist prefers gen_kernels_v2 on newer archs right now.
Nina: is the KV lease/persistence for kernel affinity persisted across driver restarts? I thought we checkpointed those to disk every 5m?
Samir: we persist affinity blobs, but the new driver binary changed the blob schema (minor version bump) and our loader falls back to safe-mode which invalidates affinity and TTLs. So after restart the system treated affinity as stale and re-autotuned.
Meera: right — loader does version check: if schema_version != runtime_expected then we invalidate to avoid mismatched kernel metadata. We should refine to support a migration or at least retain lease TTLs.
Alex: the perf regression came from two things: (1) affinity eviction caused re-probing that picked a more generic kernel for 128-256, (2) KV prefix cache warming lag — prefix cache went from 0.81 -> 0.62 after restart for that workload.
Nina: ideas for mitigation? quick wins would be: resume TTLs when schema bump is minor, and seed affinity from a read-only fallback store before re-probe.
Samir: propose this short plan: 
- change loader to classify schema bumps as major/minor. For minor: run a compatibility adapter to translate old affinity into new format and preserve TTL (fast path).
- on restart, mark affinity blobs as "probe-preferred" for 30s to avoid immediate full re-autotune.
- warm KV prefixes eagerly for top-10 hot prefixes at startup.
Meera: agree. Also add a canary flag that forces kernel probe for one percent of traffic to validate translations instead of wholesale invalidation.
Alex: I can prototype the adapter for old->new affinity mapping. Will need sample old blobs (we have archived ones in /mnt/affinity-checkpoints).
Nina: I'll add an ops playbook: if autotuner picks a slower kernel after restart, ops can flip a quick flag to restore persisted affinity (rollback TTL) until adapter lands.
Samir: testing notes: we should run a 2hr perf job that simulates sequence-length distribution skewed to 128-256 with burstiness to capture steady-state batching behavior. Include kernel-selector tracing.
Alex: adding the test to CI perf cluster now. command I'm running: 
```
perf-run --profile seqlen-skew-128-256 --trace kernel-selector --duration 7200 --report s3://redwood-perf/2298765432
```
Meera: also add a microbenchmark that measures probe cold-start cost: re-probe overhead per model variant and per arch. We want a baseline for the "probe-preferred" 30s mitigation.
Nina: ops note: make sure the playbook documents how to check "kv-prefix-warmth" metric (metric name: runtime.kv.prefix_warmth) and the affinity schema version (runtime.kernel.affinity_schema).
Alex: ok will send a follow-up with the adapter PR and perf run link once done. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Samir: leaving a reminder: when implementing adapter, log a small histogram of translated affinity hit correctness so we can catch corruption quickly.
Meera: and add an alert if cache_hit_rate drops >10% post-restart for 15m.
Nina: noted. scheduling ops window and alert updates.
Alex: end.
